The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, Seyi Makinde, has dismissed reports that he is negotiating with another candidate to withdraw from the 2027 presidential election. Makinde’s campaign organisation, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation, said in a statement on Thursday that the claim circulating on social media was false, insisting that the Oyo State governor remained committed to contesting the election. The statement, signed by the organisation’s Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Ihediwa, said Makinde was focused on winning the presidency and implementing his RESET Nigeria agenda. “Engr. Makinde is fully in the 2027 Presidential race with his RESET Nigeria Agenda on the platform of the APM. “He is focused on the Presidency to lead a four years transitional government of national unity and nothing less,” it said. It, however, did not identify the minister or provide evidence to support the allegation. The organisation also challenged President Bola Tinubu and the APC to face Makinde at the polls rather than spread claims about his withdrawal from the contest. I bought a book on how to have a son – Makinde 2027: Makinde proposes government of national unity 2027: Oyinlola dismisses claim APC will sweep South-West Makinde, who is seeking the presidency under the APM, unveiled his RESET Nigeria manifesto on November 4, outlining proposals on economic development, security, education and governance. His running mate is former Director-General of the Department of State Services, Lawal Daura. The governor has described his proposed administration as a four-year transitional government of national unity, saying it would pursue reforms to address the country’s economic and governance challenges. The 2027 presidential election is scheduled for January 16, with 18 candidates cleared by the Independent National Electoral Commission to contest the poll. They include incumbent Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress, Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress and Makinde of the APM.
